title: Telemetry-driven heuristic advisor for continuous batching and safe config rollback
creator: Priya Shah
description: Goal: Build a telemetry-driven recommendation engine that generates safe, incremental continuous-batching and KV-cache configuration proposals for production workloads and can apply them with an automated canary + rollback path. Deliverable should include an offline profiler, a scoring/heuristic layer, a runtime-safe apply flow, observability hooks, and a rollback/guardrail policy.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Offline profiler produces per-workload fingerprint and suggested batching parameters (max_batch_size, max_latency_ms, batch_timeout_ms, kv_cache_enabled, kv_cache_retention) with confidence score.
2) Heuristic advisor maps fingerprints to safe parameter ranges and a rollout plan (canary %s, monitoring windows).
3) Runtime apply supports atomic snapshot, staged canary, anomaly detection, and automatic rollback.
4) Metrics and dashboards surface cost delta, p50/p95 latency, error rate, and token-per-GPU throughput for each rollout.
5) Integration tests that simulate bursty traffic and validate rollback triggers within CI harness.
6) Human-runbook and automated postmortem signals when rollback occurs.
implementation_notes:
Architecture: (1) Workload profiler service samples request traces for 72 hours and computes sequence-length distribution, prefix-reuse rate, concurrency distribution, and kv-cache hit projections. (2) Heuristic layer applies rule-based safety gates derived from offline experiments (see design doc). (3) Runtime controller writes proposed config as a new snapshot to /configs/batching/{workload}, then triggers canary traffic routing (default 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with rolling windows.
Key heuristics: prefer smaller max_batch_size for high-latency-sensitive routes, aggressive coalescing for homogeneous short-seq workloads, disable KV-cache for low-prefix-reuse but enable for high reuse. Confidence scoring: combine KL divergence from baseline, tail-latency delta estimate, and token-cost estimate.
Rollback policy: automatic rollback if error_rate > 0.5% absolute increase OR p95 latency > 2x baseline OR cost-per-token increases > 20% sustained for 10m. Snapshotting: every apply stores previous config id and the sample metrics for diffing. Manual override available in Console.

open_questions: What is the acceptable customer-facing latency regression for P2 routes? (Engineering suggested 10% p95 cap; PM may tighten.)
Should the advisor expose a suggested 'confidence' threshold for auto-apply vs manual approval?
What's the rollout cadence default for high-volume workloads vs low-volume (e.g., 5%->25%->100% over 30m vs 24h)?
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for profiler and heuristic scoring. 2) Integration: runtime simulator replicating mixed traffic shapes (burst, steady, diurnal) and assert rollback conditions. 3) Canary: run auto-rollout on internal dev account for 2 weeks against staged load. 4) Chaos test: inject 10% upstream latency and ensure advisor does not apply destabilizing batching changes.
rollback_runbook:
- Before apply: snapshot current config and note baseline metrics (p50/p95 latency, error_rate, token_throughput).
- Apply step 1: write snapshot and set canary routing to 5% for 5m.
- Monitoring: check p95 and error_rate every 30s.
- Escalate: if automatic triggers fire, controller reverts to snapshot id and posts Slack alert to #runtime-ops with rollback reason and metrics.
- Post-rollback: collect traces for 1h, create postmortem if rollback impacted >=2 customers.
- Manual restore: UI or CLI supports re-applying previous snapshot with explicit acknowledgement.
